analysis:
Examined all supplied source, patches and metadata against the canonical definition index and selected details. No independently supported security regression is established in this scope. release-provider.yml moves staging/publication to ubuntu-24.04 (head 1211, 1320); surrounding artifact ID/digest inputs, pinned dependency installation, environment-specific credentials, serialized publication and coordinator-before-alias publication remain unchanged. This affects release custody (A-005, A-011, A-017, T-054), not provider serving authorization; signing and older-macOS smoke remain on macOS. Helper implementations were not supplied, so their unchanged contracts are not revalidated.

threat-model-review.yml now runs only for labeled events (head 6, 71), removes the one-shot label (76-82), adds issues:write and moves Linux runners. Trusted-default-branch scanner checkout and pinned clients remain; no new execution of PR source is visible. Automatic rescanning on pushes/base edits is removed. Material integration question: reconcile this with the retained conditional-clearance mode (62, 67, 172-178) and threat-review-gate.py. An unrelated label skips the review job, while subsequent pushes do not trigger it; whether this can satisfy a required rule without current-tree clearance depends on the rule/gate contract, which is not supplied. Do not infer an active deployment or a proven bypass.

The changelog (3-6) and build.md patch (head 360-396) describe opt-in tests, removal of hourly coverage, tree-based reuse, retry and watchdog changes. These are documentation evidence, not proof of implementation correctness. Integration should validate CI filtering/reuse and required-check behavior across ci-dev.yml, ci-master.yml, ci-tested-tree.py, routing/watchdog and release diff gates, especially preserving exact artifact qualification and availability (A-017/A-018). No runtime encryption, cache, billing, privileged-helper or plaintext-handling change appears here.
